correctness.rationale: Parseval fixes the exact loss. Direct subtraction yields Δ_N=2/3−1/[3N(N+1)]−4 S_N/[N(N+1)]; weighted averaging of decreasing Fourier heat coefficients makes Δ_N strictly increasing in N. For each N it strictly increases with time and has one zero, giving all optimal orders and adjacent ties. Euler–Maclaurin with nonzero I1 derivative proves t_N=u*/[N(N+1)]+O(N^-4); Riemann sums and strictly monotone limiting derivative give the sharp positive J*; a separate norm decomposition gives the 2/(3t) moment-match penalty. The included standard-library checker passed 1124 finite diagnostics, which corroborate but are not substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: Fejér means are the canonical nonnegative finite Fourier tapers; selecting their bandwidth to emulate heat smoothing is a natural spectral-calibration problem. The result determines ALL exact finite-time optimal integers and tie cases, a sharp universal small-time scale and error, and proves that the naive first-moment matching scale is asymptotically wrong with an unbounded squared-error penalty. These are nontrivial global structural and quantitative facts, rather than a single routine finite computation.
